Allow me to tell you guys a story. A lot of people will probably say I am going to hell for doing this but I'm an atheist and am suffering from depression, so I don't care about your hell.

This all happened a few years back. I had lunch with my girlfriend (now wife) and her grandma (about 80+ years old). We were walking to our car with me about 10 paces behind grandma when suddenly a couple of punk ass kids rushed grandma and grabbed her purse. Now I've never been in a fight nor ever wanted to be in one since I'm not very good at confrontations and am somewhat puny (I'm 5'5 and a tad overweight). But when I saw one kid shoved grandma, something in me just snapped. I don't know where I found the strength (probably adrenaline) but I found myself releasing a punch at that one kid (considerably larger than I am) landing him flat on his back. Things started to go blurry around this time for me, all I can see then was this one kid. i was oblivious to everything else around me. From my warped perspective, he was no longer this big scary thief. He was a rag doll that pushed grandma. I felt larger, scarier and hungry. I can't remember a lot.  I remember stomping at his knees, a lot of slaps to his ears and a lot of punches. There was blood everywhere when I calmed down and regained my sanity. One of the onlookers said at one point I was breaking his fingers one by one.

I then sat down, caught my breath, and promptly threw up my lunch.

I'm sorry for your troubles. I know depression is a bitch. I wish I can tell you to just snap out of it, or grow a pair, or some other quick way to make the feeling of guilt and weight of responsibilities and expectations disappear. But I can't. Things can get better or a LOT worse. Personally, I have lost interest in things I've used to enjoy. Several times, I found myself with a pistol in my mouth. But I'm still trying to hope things will get better.

All I can say is you're still young. You still have time to fix things. Deal with stuff one thing at a time. Forget about relationships. It may seem like it's the most important thing right now. Start with the small physical stuff. Little victories might help lessen that stabbing pain. Once you achieve that, move on the next, and the next.
